title: Doubles in the Upper Tail
problem: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. Given that their sum is at least 10, what is the probability that the dice show the same number?

hints.text: List the ordered pairs whose sums satisfy the information you were given.
There are three ordered pairs summing to 10, two summing to 11, and one summing to 12.

solution.setup: Condition on the six ordered outcomes with sum at least 10.
solution.reasoning: The eligible ordered pairs are (4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), and (6,6). Because the original 36 ordered pairs are equally likely, these six remain equally likely after conditioning. The favorable pairs are (5,5) and (6,6), so the probability is 2/6.
solution.sanityCheck: The conditional probability is much larger than the unconditional doubles probability 1/6 because the high-sum condition keeps both high doubles while discarding most non-doubles.

keyInsight: When the original elementary outcomes are equally likely, conditioning lets you count favorable outcomes inside the restricted set.
recognitionCues: A condition on the sum restricts which ordered dice outcomes are possible.
commonMistakes: Treating the sums 10, 11, and 12 as equally likely rather than counting their ordered realizations.
followUps: Given that the sum is at least 9, what is the probability of doubles?

source.notes: Original exercise based on standard finite sample-space reasoning.

verification.notes: Six qualifying ordered pairs; exactly two are doubles.
